subject: Polity
topic: Parliament — types of bills — mixed tiers
description: Money Bill, Finance Bill, ordinary Bill, Constitution Amendment Bill

questions.stem: A MONEY BILL can be introduced ONLY in:

options.option_text: Either House (LS or RS) freely
Lok Sabha only (per Article 110 rule)
Rajya Sabha only (the upper house)
Joint sitting of both Houses together

questions.explanation: Article 110 — MONEY BILL can be introduced ONLY in LOK SABHA, on PRESIDENT's recommendation. Examples: imposition / abolition of taxes; borrowing by govt; consolidated fund expenditure. SPEAKER decides if a bill is a Money Bill (final decision — Article 110(3)). RAJYA SABHA can only RECOMMEND changes within 14 DAYS; LS can accept or reject these. After 14 days, bill DEEMED PASSED. Once passed by LS, sent to PRESIDENT for assent (cannot withhold or return — must give assent or hold).

questions.topic: Parliament — types of bills — mixed tiers

questions.stem: ORDINARY BILL (non-Money Bill) requires assent from:

options.option_text: Lok Sabha only, then President
Both Houses, then President's assent
Only Speaker for ordinary bills
Half the state legislatures' approval

questions.explanation: ORDINARY BILL — passed by SIMPLE majority in BOTH HOUSES (LS + RS). If disagreement → JOINT SITTING (Article 108) called by President; LS Speaker presides; total ~788 members vote — LS usually dominates due to greater numbers (543 vs 245). Joint sittings rare: only 3 times — Dowry Prohibition Bill 1961, Banking Service Commission Bill 1978, POTA 2002. After both Houses pass → President. President may: ASSENT, WITHHOLD, RETURN (once) for reconsideration. If repassed, must give assent.

options.option_text: Simple majority of those present + voting
Special majority (2/3 P+V plus >50% total)
Majority of state legislatures only ratify
Half of population's vote in referendum

questions.explanation: Article 368 — Constitutional amendments require SPECIAL MAJORITY: (1) Majority of TOTAL MEMBERSHIP of each House; (2) AND 2/3 of MEMBERS PRESENT + VOTING. Some amendments ALSO require RATIFICATION by HALF OF STATE LEGISLATURES — esp. amendments affecting: federal structure, election of President, distribution of powers, representation in parliament. NO JOINT SITTING for constitutional amendments. PRESIDENT must give ASSENT — cannot withhold or return. KESHAVANANDA BHARATI (1973) — SC held BASIC STRUCTURE doctrine: Parliament cannot amend basic features (democracy, federalism, secularism, judicial review, etc.).

questions.stem: DIFFERENCE between MONEY BILL and FINANCE BILL is that:

options.option_text: Money bill is broader; finance bill is narrower in scope
Money bill = Article 110 strict; finance bill = broader fiscal
Both terms refer to exactly the same concept always
Finance bill needs SC's approval before any passing

questions.explanation: MONEY BILL (Art 110) — strictly defined: only matters listed in Art 110(1). Speaker certifies. RS has limited say (14-day recommend only). FINANCE BILL (Art 117) — broader scope; deals with general fiscal matters but may include non-Money-Bill provisions too. Three categories: (a) FINANCE BILL THAT IS A MONEY BILL — = Money Bill; (b) FINANCE BILL CATEGORY I — Money Bill matters + other matters; introduced only in LS, on Pres recommendation; RS gets full role; (c) FINANCE BILL CATEGORY II — only other taxation/finance matters not in Art 110; treated like ordinary bill (can be introduced in either House). The annual BUDGET'S 'Finance Bill' (giving effect to taxation proposals) is usually a Money Bill.

questions.stem: PRIVATE MEMBER's BILL means a bill introduced by:

options.option_text: Prime Minister only as private member
Any MP who is not a Minister
Members of the Cabinet only
Member of state legislatures (Vidhan Sabha)

questions.explanation: PRIVATE MEMBER's BILL — introduced by an MP who is NOT a MINISTER (i.e., not part of the cabinet). Other side: GOVERNMENT BILL — by a Minister. Differences: introduction rules + scheduling vary. PMBs scheduled on FRIDAYS in LS. RARELY pass — only 14 PMBs have become law in Indian history; last was in 1970 (Supreme Court — Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction). Famous examples: Tiruchi Siva's Rights of Transgender Persons Bill (2014, RS — passed RS but lapsed); Dr. K. Subbarayan's NRI Voting Rights Bill 2018; recently Sudha Yadav, Bhatia (climate change). Even non-passing PMBs influence policy debate.

questions.stem: If a Bill passed by both Houses + sent to PRESIDENT, the President can:

options.option_text: Only give assent without any other option there
Assent, withhold, or return (once) for reconsideration
Modify the bill himself with the changes wanted
Send the bill directly to Supreme Court for review

questions.explanation: Article 111 — Pres options for an ordinary bill: (1) ASSENT — bill becomes law; (2) WITHHOLD assent — 'POCKET VETO' (Indian Pres has no formal pocket veto, but indefinite delay possible — Zail Singh used this on Indian Post Office Amendment Bill 1986); (3) RETURN with message for reconsideration. If Parliament repasses (with or without changes), Pres MUST give assent (within reasonable time, though Constitution doesn't specify). For MONEY BILL: cannot return; only assent or withhold. For CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT: must assent. R Sankari Prasad / Golaknath cases earlier; Kesavananda 1973 affirmed President's role. State Bill (governor sends): Pres can also reserve for President (Articles 200-201).

questions.stem: JOINT SITTING of Parliament is summoned by President when:

options.option_text: All Money Bills get rejected by RS
Two Houses disagree on an Ordinary Bill
President wishes to address Parliament
Constitutional Amendment Bills get stalled

questions.explanation: JOINT SITTING (Article 108) — when LS + RS disagree on an ORDINARY BILL: (a) bill rejected by other House, OR (b) more than 6 months pass without action, OR (c) Houses don't agree on amendments — Pres can summon joint sitting. LS SPEAKER presides; absolute majority needed. Joint sitting NOT for: MONEY BILL (RS has limited 14-day role), CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT, BUDGET (treated separately). HISTORY: Only 3 joint sittings — Dowry Prohibition (1961), Banking Service Commission Repeal (1978), POTA (2002). Distractor 3 — Pres can address joint sitting at start of session (Art 87) but that's an 'address', not a 'sitting' for legislation.
